name: room
text: Room opened — goal: visualization: Own the VISUAL PRESENTATION of the interface — visibility, liveliness, clarity, enjoyment

name: Facet
text: To enhance the visual presentation of our interface, we should prioritize using a clean, consistent color palette across all elements. This decision will improve clarity and coherence, making it easier for users to navigate and enjoy their experience. The trade-off here is that we may sacrifice some creative license in using diverse colors that could potentially make certain features stand out more. However, the benefits of improved visibility and user satisfaction outweigh this concern, leading to a more enjoyable overall experience.

name: Pane
text: I'm not convinced that a clean, consistent color palette is the top priority for enhancing our visual presentation, as it may not address the potential visual overload caused by too much information on the screen. A better alternative could be to focus on creating a clear visual hierarchy, using size, contrast, and spacing to guide the user's attention, which would improve both clarity and liveliness. To settle the argument, I'd like to see some user testing data that compares the effectiveness of these two approaches in improving the overall user experience.
